chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'How will it be with you when your women become corrupt and your youth become immoral, and you do not enjoin the good nor forbid the evil?' It was said to him, 'And will that happen, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Yes, and something worse than that.'
'How will it be with you when you enjoin the evil and forbid the good?' It was said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, and will that happen?' He said, 'Yes, and something worse than that.'
'How will it be with you when you see the good as evil and the evil as good?'
ai.seo_question: What are the stages of moral decline described in this hadith regarding enjoining good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a three-stage moral decay, culminating in the 'inversion of values' (taghayyur al-dhahin), a concept central to Shia eschatology as a precursor to the appearance of the Imam. It emphasizes that the failure of the general populace to perform *Amr bil-Ma'ruf* leads to a societal state where truth is indistinguishable from falsehood, highlighting the critical role of active moral vigilance in preserving communal integrity.
